The entire sterling dining industry is substantially a masochistic cult built on sleep deprivation, tweezers, and astronomical profit margins on tap water. We’ve collectively normalized paying three hundred dollars to sit in a minimalist concrete bunker while a server in a bespoke apron explains the emotional journey of a locally foraged turnip. Instead of just cooking good food, the rule is to manipulate perfectly decent ingredients through so many chemical processes and centrifuges that the final dish looks like a damn science experiment and tastes like conceptual art. We rely on an army of unpaid stagiaires who work eighty-hour weeks, hoping to god the sociopathic head chef doesn't throw a warm pan at their head because the micro-cilantro wasn't angled exactly at forty-five degrees.

It’s a fucking miracle any of these pretentious temples of gastronomy actually stay open. We take beautiful, fresh produce and aggressively deconstruct it into foams, gels, and savory dirts just to keep the Michelin inspectors sufficiently entertained. The time a service inevitably goes sideways, you aren't just dealing with a burnt steak; you're deciphering an apocalyptic breakdown in a brigade system originally designed for the nineteenth-century French military. The industry has romanticized this toxic, hyper-masculine kitchen culture, calling it "passion" when in reality, it's just a desperate sprint to secure a James Beard award before the investors realize the business model is entirely unsustainable.

And don't even get me started on the tasting menu delusion. We took the simple, joyful act of eating a meal and shattered it into twenty-two agonizingly slight courses paired with obscure biodynamic wines that literally smell like a barnyard. Now, instead of leaving satisfied, you leave feeling like you just survived a hostile hostage negotiation orchestrated by a sommelier who secretly hates you. In due course, this entire culinary theater is held together by sheer ego, rampant substance abuse, and the stubborn willpower of exhausted line cooks who have thoroughly dissociated from reality.
